submission.hypothesis: The exact public admission boundary is that `workspace.execBound` structurally fixes immutable-input execution to `contained_local` (its MCP adapter calls `bind_bound`, which forces `ExecutionProfile::ContainedLocal` and suppresses any caller-selectable `executionProfile`), while `windows_native` admission is gated in Core (`validate_run_structure`, engine.rs:4914-4927) to `TrustedLocal` with zero steps. These two Runtime-owned fact sets are mutually exclusive by construction: there is no `windows_native` + `contained_local` combination the public surface can express, so a real cross-target workload that wants to keep canonical source bytes and `foreignReferences` while dispatching on `windows_native` cannot pass `workspace.execBound` at all.
submission.causalMechanism: 1) `workspace.exec_bound` (tools.rs:631-643) calls `bind_bound`, whose test (`workspace_exec_bound_binding_forces_contained_local`, tests.rs:220-260) asserts the resulting proposal has `execution_profile == ContainedLocal`. The `WorkspaceExecBoundExecution` schema explicitly omits `executionProfile` (tests.rs:170-172), so the caller cannot override it. 2) On the Core side, `validate_run_structure` (engine.rs:4914) rejects any `execution_profile != TrustedLocal` when `execution_target == WindowsNative` with `"windows_native currently supports trusted_local only"` (engine.rs:4917), and also rejects multi-step for windows_native (engine.rs:4921). Therefore any `execBound` proposal (always `ContainedLocal`) reaching Core with `executionTarget=WindowsNative` fails that validation before admission. The immutable-input materialization presented read-only under /run/ordivon/inputs is per docs also described only in contained_local terms (`effect-kernel.md:187`, `agent-ux.md:15`), so the boundary is owned by Runtime in two coupled places: (a) the MCP Tool's structural profile freeze, and (b) Core's windows_native profile/steps reservation. Neither byte authority nor path authority is in World/Agent arguments; the executable/argv/env/foreignReferences remain concrete action input carried through the same proposal-plus-input identity.
submission.nextFalsifier: The smallest next physical falsifier without moving byte/path authority into World or Agent arguments: build a real WSL/Windows provider and a real cross-target fixture that admits one `windows_native` single-command Job through the existing documented path but with immutable inputs, to demonstrate whether the blocker is (i) the `bind_bound` profile freeze at the MCP layer (would need a Core-side admission contract permitting `contained_local` semantics for windows_native), or (ii) the Core `windows_native currently supports trusted_local only` gate (engine.rs:4917) as the sole boundary. Keep the caller submitting only authority name + relativeObject + expectedDigest + presentationRelativePath, keep `contained_local` semantics for input materialization, and do NOT add any host-source-path argument; the falsifier is a deterministic admission test asserting whether the current two-hop profile/step guard, not a schema or identity change, is what blocks the combined workload.
